newsitem.title: USA: Rubin, Mitsuzuka oppose excess forex volatility.
newsitem.headline: Rubin, Mitsuzuka oppose excess forex volatility.

text.p: U.S. Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin and Japanese Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka agreed on Friday that excess currency market volatility was undesirable, a Treasury spokesman said.
At a bilateral meeting ahead of the Group of Seven summit here, the two men also agreed to continue to cooperate closely in currency markets as appropriate, the spokesman added.
"The two ministers agreed that excess volatility of exchange rates is undesirable," he said. "They reaffirmed their commitment to cooperate closely in exchange markets as appropriate."

At the meeting, Mitsuzuka reaffirmed Japan's objective of promoting strong domestic demand-led economic growth and avoiding a significant increase in its trade surplus, the U.S. Treasury spokesman said.
The Japanese minister also voiced his determination to push ahead with plans for wide-ranging reform of Japan's financial system, while ensuring its stabilty and strengthening it.
"Secretary Rubin welcomed the Japanese government's commitment to deregulation, to financial reform and to strengthening the banking system,"the Treasury spokesman added.
